first_impression.reaction: Typed 'mykonos wedding' on the train. The first paragraph tells me it's three decisions in order: legal or symbolic, season, then area and venue. Fine, I know what this page is. No pop-up. The takeaways are short, but none of them actually tells me a month or a venue, so I scroll. I'd jump to the venue shortlist and the weather table, glance at the FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: A Mykonos wedding comes down to three decisions, made in order: whether the ceremony is legal or symbolic, which starts the paperwork clock; the season, read from official climate figures and current travel advice; and the area and kind of venue that suit your guest list.
journey.reaction: Clear enough. Three things, in order. I know where to scroll.

journey.quote: Read the season from the figures for Naxos, the nearest official weather station, and plan ceremony times around summer heat and the north wind.
journey.reaction: Wait, Naxos? I searched Mykonos. And it tells me how to pick a month, not which month. This is the one takeaway I wanted an answer from.

journey.quote: Ask every venue about deposits, cancellation, exclusive use and music times, and get the answers in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Practical. Hadn't thought about music times at all.

journey.section: Why couples choose Mykonos for their wedding
journey.quote: Mykonos sits in the heart of the Cyclades and is known as the island of the winds.
journey.reaction: I already picked Mykonos, that's why I searched it. Scrolling past.

journey.section: Areas of the island and what each suits
journey.quote: Think about the island in terms of the evening you want rather than a map.
journey.reaction: Nice way to put it. Town, beach or sunset, I can pick one in a second.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: Ceremonies take place on The Ocean Balcony, just above Psarou beach, for up to 60 guests, and the wedding party can then move to the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area for up to 120.
journey.reaction: Real names, real numbers. This is the bit I'd screenshot.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: The hotel describes its weddings as running from intimate gatherings to large weddings with up to 800 guests, from welcome cocktails to five-course gala dinners.
journey.reaction: 800! Didn't expect that on an island. Good to know there's range.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact, start to finish, and confirms the unpublished details above and every inclusion in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: I'm just looking. Not clicking yet, but it didn't get in my way.

journey.quote: | Month (Naxos station) | Mean °C | Mean maximum °C | Rain (mm) | Rain days |
journey.reaction: Five columns on my phone means scrolling sideways, and two temperature columns side by side take a second to work out.

journey.quote: From June to August, rain all but disappears at Naxos, with under one rain day a month in July and August.
journey.reaction: OK, this is the answer I wanted. It should have been in the takeaways.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller's advice for Greece](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) is to exercise normal safety precautions.
journey.reaction: Dated this year. That's the 'is this still true?' question answered. Bold lead-ins make the list easy to thumb through.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at many Australian embassies and consulates overseas, or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney; a fee applies.
journey.reaction: This whole section is Australian paperwork. I'm in Singapore. Clearly labelled, so I skip it, but it's a lot of scrolling on a phone.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Proper checklist. This is what I'd bookmark and send to my partner.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Mykonos wedding
journey.quote: The cost of a Mykonos wedding moves with the decisions above, not with the island alone.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it costs. No number, but the headings at least show what pushes the bill up.

journey.quote: A legal ceremony is one of your two routes.
journey.reaction: I asked 'can you legally get married in Mykonos?' Is that a yes? Just say yes first.

journey.quote: At Naxos, the nearest official weather station, June to August are driest, while October brings the most rain of those months and the north wind runs stronger from July to October.
journey.reaction: Better than most FAQs, it gives months. Still doesn't say which months suit a wedding best, I have to work it out.

journey.quote: Yes. Many couples complete the legal step in Australia, then hold a symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, first word. That's what I want from every FAQ.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Mykonos wedding cost? Even a ballpark.
So which month would the guide actually pick for a wedding? It gives the data but never says it plainly.
How far ahead do these venues book out?
Is the Wedded Advisor service for people outside Australia too?

turn_offs_found.quote: Read the season from the figures for Naxos, the nearest official weather station, and plan ceremony times around summer heat and the north wind.
turn_offs_found.why: The takeaways are the only part I'm sure to read. This one tells me how to choose a season instead of naming months, and leading with another island's name in a Mykonos takeaway makes me stop and wonder if I'm on the right page. The useful line about June to August sits under the table.

turn_offs_found.quote: A legal ceremony is one of your two routes.
turn_offs_found.why: I often jump straight to the FAQ. My question is yes or no, and the answer doesn't start with either, so I have to read the whole thing to be sure.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Month (Naxos station) | Mean °C | Mean maximum °C | Rain (mm) | Rain days |
turn_offs_found.why: Five columns on a phone means sideways scrolling, and 'Mean °C' next to 'Mean maximum °C' makes me stop and figure out which one matters. Minor, the sentences under it help.

turn_offs_found.quote: Mykonos sits in the heart of the Cyclades and is known as the island of the winds.
turn_offs_found.why: Minor. A scene-setting section sits between the takeaways and the venues, one more screen before the useful bit. Not a deal-breaker because the intro already told me where to go.

would_share_with: My partner: the five-venue shortlist and the house rules checklist
A friend comparing Greek islands: the area breakdown and the ferry and wind notes

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Mykonos wedding with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I'm only researching. No pop-ups, links stayed out of my way, so no complaint. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and 'quotes in AUD' makes me unsure they'd take someone in Singapore.

top_3_changes: Name the months in the season takeaway (for example, June to August driest, May and September milder), so the takeaways answer 'when' without the reader scrolling to the table.
Open the 'Can you legally get married in Mykonos?' FAQ with a plain 'Yes', then the two routes.
Make the weather table easier on a phone, for example by dropping one of the two temperature columns, and put the June to August line directly above it.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Title, deferred business details and deliberately unprinted prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing or not-published explanations

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'mykonos wedding' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, skimmed 'Why couples choose', read the areas and venue shortlist, the weather section, skipped most of the Australian legal detail, read the house rules, skimmed costs, then the FAQ.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question and a low objection only.
The title, fees and company specifics (including the AUD and Australian focus) are deferred, so they are noted as reader reactions but kept out of top_3_changes.
Image slots, HTML comments and any [[VERIFY]] markers treated as invisible.
Quotes are given as a reader sees them, with inline HTML fact comments removed; link markup kept where the quoted sentence contains a link.
